note: Squarely good-to-great on substance: 182 lb at six feet, plays tennis and golf, swims, swings a kettlebell two or three times a week, and describes himself as 'skinny fat' wanting muscle and less visceral fat rather than rescue. Health is the classic neglected corner — 'I preach other people about health, but I haven't been applying it on myself' — and the pneumonia and shingles this year were what finally moved him. He clears the deconditioned exclusion easily. Both misses are about what was never established or what he declined: his occupation was never asked once in a 61-minute call, which is the fifth time in this batch, and he bought the $1,000 entry tier having cited finances as part of the reason ('It's a little bit financial'). The pattern worth carrying up is that this prospect looks like the ICP on every dimension the criteria describe and still transacted at one sixth of the headline price — which is the same observation the existing ICP notes make about income failing to predict willingness to pay.
